# S239 — Check failures: show the failing tests to the fix round and run a failed check once more before sending it

*Proposed.* When the project check command fails, ork runs it once more before it starts a fix round. If the rerun passes, the round is not spent and the run record says the check was flaky. If it fails again, the fix-round brief starts with the failing test names and their assertion lines (bounded), then the output tail as before.

**Findings:**  · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

Observed on S207's fix round (wave 4, 2026-11-02, `.scratch/v11/wave4-friction.md`, F23 to F25).

1. The excerpt had no failing assertion (F23). Verified in code: a red check goes to `bumpRound` with the log as feedback (`internal/engine/states.go:170-171`). The brief for it is the last 30000 bytes of the log (`states.go:109-110`), and the log holds the last 30000 bytes of the command's stdout plus stderr, then `slicer check --json` (`states.go:213`, `:222`). There is no step that looks for `--- FAIL` lines. So a header and assertion that sit earlier than the last 30000 bytes of output (for example before a race report or a timeout panic with its goroutine dump) are dropped. The landing re-check brief does the same (`internal/engine/land.go:175`). *Not verified:* what the S207 log held, because run logs live in `~/.local/state/ork/runs/` (outside this workspace, not read). The implementer's own words (it could not see the failing assertion, so it asked whether the fix round may edit the TUI and daemon files S207 excludes) are the only evidence of what the brief showed.
2. The failure did not reproduce (F24). The orchestrator ran the two packages alone in the S207 worktree, and both passed: without `-race` `internal/daemon` 47.0s and `internal/tui` 3.8s (`.scratch/v11/s207-dt.out`), with `-race` 78.2s and 39.9s (`.scratch/v11/s207-dt-race.out`). The code runs the check once and treats a red result as final (`states.go:192-241`). `RunCheck` knows only OK or not (`internal/engine/check.go:19-33`, `CheckOutput` at `internal/engine/engine.go:29-32`), so a timeout and an exit failure look the same to `runChecks`. Each wasted fix round also spends one of the run's implementer rounds (`bumpRound` stops at `DefaultMaxRounds`, 8; `internal/engine/engine.go:26`).
3. Load (F25). Verified: a run counts against the global cap (default 2, adj 172) while its engine goroutine is busy, and that includes the checks step (`hasRoomLocked`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:793-813`, adj 122); approve, answer and retry bypass the cap, and nothing makes a check wait for another run's check or for other work on the machine (landing alone has a lock, `internal/engine/landlock.go`). *Not verified:* what was running at the time and whether a timing test was the cause; the log says "likely" (F25). So this slice does not change admission; it adds the rerun, which is the cheap answer to a failure that load caused, and asks the owner whether checks should also wait.

`checks.deterministic` (adj 31, decided) says ork runs the check command and `slicer check` after the implementer and red goes back without a review; a rerun keeps that rule. No slicer feature covers this (`slicer find rerun`, `slicer find flaky` list nothing relevant) and the check command is ork's to run (`docs/design.md:288-292`). `S234` and its discovered-from list name this friction as "check failures"; this is the slice.

Owner decisions (interactive question, 2026-11-02): the fix-round brief gets a Go-test-aware excerpt of at most 8000 bytes before the existing 30000-byte tail; the project check command is rerun once after an exit failure, not after a timeout and not for the slicer check; a pass on the rerun is recorded as flaky in `run.json` and the log only; making checks wait for other runs is not part of this slice.

## Implement

The steps follow the owner's answers of 2026-11-02 (see the lead section). Re-anchor every line number with `rg -n` first.

1. Tests first, in the order above. Run them and see each named failure.
2. `CheckOutput` gets `TimedOut bool`. `RunCheck` sets it in the `TimeoutError` branch only (`check.go:29-30`). Keep the existing output text.
3. `internal/engine/failures.go`, `FailureExcerpt(output, limit)`: go through the lines once. Keep (a) every line whose text after leading spaces starts `--- FAIL:`, with the lines under it that are indented deeper than it, at most 20 lines per test; (b) `FAIL` and `FAIL<TAB>` package lines; (c) a `panic: ` line and the five lines after it; (d) a `WARNING: DATA RACE` line and the lines after it up to a blank line, at most 25; (e) `# ` package lines and `FILE.go:N:N: message` lines. Cut a line to 400 bytes at a rune boundary and add `...`. Stop at `limit` bytes on a whole line and append `[N more failing tests not shown]`. Return the test names from the `--- FAIL:` lines in order, without repeats. Return `"", nil` when no `--- FAIL`, `panic:`, `DATA RACE` or build-error line was found. Use the standard library only. Go `-json` output is not parsed.
4. `internal/engine/states.go` `runChecks`: after the first project-command run, when the result is not OK, `TimedOut` is false and the run was not cancelled, run the same command once more with the same directory and timeout. If the rerun cannot run, pause as the first run would. Write the log as the first run's `tail(output, 30000)` and, under a line `$ COMMAND (run again once: the first run failed)`, the second run's. Do not rerun `slicer check`. Set `ok` from the second result. Record `Attempts` 2, and `Flaky` true when the first failed and the second passed; `Seconds` stays the whole time of the step. A passing first run records neither field.
5. The `checks` brief (`states.go:109-110`) and the landing brief (`land.go:173-177`): build the body with one helper, for example `checkFailureBody(log string) string`. When `FailureExcerpt(log, 8000)` is not empty the body is the line "The failing tests and assertion lines, cut to fit:", the excerpt in a fence, then "The end of the output:" and the existing `tail(log, 30000)` in a fence. When the log shows two runs, add one line that the check failed in both runs, and, if the first run's test names are not all in the second's, "Failed on the first run only: NAMES." When the excerpt is empty the body is what it is today.
6. `internal/runrec/record.go`: `Attempts int json:"attempts,omitempty"` and `Flaky bool json:"flaky,omitempty"` on `CheckRecord`; no store version change (`omitempty` keys; older readers ignore them).
7. Docs: `docs/design.md:288-292` and `:506-509` (one rerun of the project command on an exit failure; the brief shows failing tests first), `docs/guide.md:254`, `docs/state.md` (the `checks[]` example at `:223` and one sentence for `attempts` and `flaky`). Mark the rerun and the excerpt *proposed*.
8. Do not touch: `internal/tui`, `internal/cli`, the admission code in `internal/daemon/runs.go`, the check timeout (`CheckMinutes`), `slicer check`, or any retry of a role.
9. Add the CHANGELOG entry last, as the first item under `## Unreleased`, marked *proposed*.
